goalTitleEN: Detect ammonium as a protein degradation product
goalDescriptionDE: Die lernende Person kann einen kontrollierten Ammonium-Nachweis über Ammoniakfreisetzung durchführen und mit der Säure-Base-Reaktion erklären sowie Befunde im Kontext von Proteinabbau begrenzt deuten.
goalDescriptionEN: The learner can carry out a controlled ammonium assay through ammonia release, explain its acid-base reaction and interpret results within bounded protein-degradation contexts.

findings.actualPixelObservation: The exposed LEFT tip above the left beaker opening is blue; the short RIGHT portion held by the forceps is pink. NH3-labelled rising schematic arrows identify the gas path adjacent to the blue exposed tip. The blue/pink distinction remains clear at 360px.
Both papers stay above their liquid surfaces. The positive blue tip sits above the open beaker rim. The image visibly says to hold the moist paper over the opening and not immerse it.
The water-control strip is entirely pink and explicitly labelled bleibt rosa. This contrasts unambiguously with the positive blue strip; no blue reaction mark appears on the control strip.

NH4+ + OH− → NH3 + H2O has correct subscripts and charges and is balanced for N=1, H=5, O=1 and net charge 0 on each side. NH3 labels the released gas; NH4+ labels the detected ion in the inference limit. No volatile NH4+ ion is implied.

The shared large panel Feuchtes Papier / Über die Öffnung halten! / Nicht eintauchen! can be read directly at actual 360×203 and 680×383 display size. It supplies the required moist-paper condition and clearly distinguishes gas detection from dipping into a basic solution.

The two-line bottom panel NH4+ nachgewiesen. / Proteinabbau nicht bewiesen. is prominent and directly legible at actual 360px. It preserves the scientific limitation: a positive assay identifies the tested ammonium condition, without establishing a protein-degradation history.

At actual unzoomed 360×203 Chromium display the equation, free-tip colour, moisture/over-opening/no-dip instructions and protein-inference limit are readable. The concise apparatus labels are smaller but also readable. The previous essential-text legibility problem is resolved; no tiny paragraph is required to understand the assay.
At actual 680×383 Chromium display all important labels and chemical notation are clear. Diagram and panels remain within the displayed image without cropping of relevant assay elements.

The image remains a friendly, uncluttered Q2 chemistry orientation illustration for exactly the controlled ammonium assay and bounded inference. No unrelated curriculum content, technical identifier, watermark or copied worksheet is visible. The removed molecular model and dense explanatory paragraphs are not required for this orientation image.

Blue arrow shapes represent schematic gas motion. The diagram does not label ammonia as a blue gas; the negative-control wisps are unlabelled pale illustrative marks and its pink-paper result stays explicit. NH3 is chemically colourless.

The far-right control forceps handle exits the image edge, contrary to the prompt request to keep all forceps within the frame. The gripping jaw, entire pink exposed paper, beaker and result label remain visible and clear; this cosmetic prompt deviation does not obscure or misrepresent the test.

The unchanged sealed goal alt text correctly covers the reaction, ammonia reaching moist indicator above the vessel, and water control without a blue change. It remains semantically compatible with this simplified image. Adding the readable inference limit to future alt text could improve completeness; no canonical metadata is modified here.
